concept.name: Live trading
concept.definition: Execution of a strategy using current market data and real orders, capital, fills, fees, and operational constraints.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Receive streaming data, create and route orders, handle asynchronous fills and failures, update portfolio state, and monitor risk controls.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A live limit order receives two partial fills and the strategy updates its remaining quantity after each broker event.
